stories.text: Mrs. Okafor opened her bakery on Mill Street at six o'clock every morning. On Tuesday the oven would not heat, so she called her nephew Emeka, who repaired machines in the next town. He arrived on a red bicycle with a bag of tools and found a loose wire behind the oven door. While he worked, Mrs. Okafor sold yesterday's bread at half price to the waiting customers. By nine o'clock the oven was hot again, and the first loaves of fresh bread came out golden. To thank him, she gave Emeka a box of six honey cakes.
qs: How many honey cakes did she give Emeka?

stories.text: Captain Ingrid Lindqvist steered the fishing boat Sea Lark out of the harbor before dawn. The radio warned that a storm would reach the coast by noon, so she decided to fish near the islands instead of the open sea. Her crew, two brothers named Jonas and Erik, pulled in the nets three times before the wind grew strong. They caught mostly cod and a few mackerel. When dark clouds gathered in the west, the captain turned the boat toward home. The Sea Lark reached the harbor just as the first heavy rain began to fall.
qs: What was the name of the boat?
Why did the captain fish near the islands?
a storm would reach the coast by noon
two brothers named jonas and erik
How many times did they pull in the nets?
Which fish did they catch mostly?

stories.text: Priya Raman spent two weekends building a small windmill for the school science fair. She made the blades from an old plastic bottle and fixed them to a wooden stick with glue. Her teacher, Mr. Delgado, suggested that she connect the windmill to a tiny light bulb. On the day of the fair, the gym was crowded with parents and students. When Priya switched on a fan, the blades turned and the bulb glowed softly. The judges gave her the second prize, a blue ribbon and a book about energy.
qs: What did she make the blades from?
Which prize did the judges give her?
a blue ribbon and a book about energy

stories.text: Every Saturday Mr. Tanaka walked to the fish market with his old dog, Kuma. This week the market was busier than usual because a festival was starting in the afternoon. While Mr. Tanaka was paying for some squid, Kuma slipped out of his collar and disappeared between the stalls. A young woman selling flowers saw the dog sniffing at a crate of tuna near the river gate. She tied a ribbon around his neck and led him back. Mr. Tanaka thanked her and bought a bunch of yellow tulips from her stall.
qs: Why was the market busier than usual?
a festival was starting in the afternoon
What was Mr. Tanaka paying for when Kuma escaped?
Where did the woman see the dog?
What did Mr. Tanaka buy from her stall?

stories.text: Dr. Leila Haddad worked at a small clinic in a mountain village. One January night, heavy snow closed the only road to the valley. At midnight a farmer named Yusuf knocked on her door because his daughter had a high fever. Dr. Haddad packed her bag, put on her boots, and followed him through the snow to his house on the hill. She gave the girl medicine and stayed beside her until morning. By sunrise the fever had dropped, and Yusuf made the doctor a cup of sweet mint tea.
qs: at a small clinic in a mountain village
Why did Yusuf knock on her door?
his daughter had a high fever
What did Yusuf make for the doctor?
a cup of sweet mint tea

stories.text: Aunt Rosa drove the whole family to the stadium to watch her son Mateo play in the youth football final. The match started at three o'clock under a grey sky. The other team scored first, and for a long time it looked as if Mateo's team would lose. Ten minutes before the end, Mateo ran down the left side and passed the ball to his friend Diego, who kicked it into the net. In extra time Mateo scored the winning goal with his head. Aunt Rosa cheered so loudly that she lost her voice.
qs: Who drove the family to the stadium?
What time did the match start?
Who kicked the ball into the net after Mateo's pass?
How did Mateo score the winning goal?
Why did Aunt Rosa lose her voice?

stories.text: On the morning before the New Year, Grandma Mei taught her grandchildren how to make dumplings. Lin chopped cabbage while his sister Hua mixed the pork with ginger and soy sauce. Grandma Mei rolled the dough into thin circles, and each child folded the filling inside. Hua's dumplings were neat, but Lin's kept opening in the boiling water. Grandma Mei laughed and showed him how to pinch the edges firmly. By evening they had made more than a hundred dumplings, enough for the whole family.
qs: Who taught the children to make dumplings?
What did Hua mix with the pork?
How many dumplings had they made by evening?

stories.text: Mr. Abebe planned to travel from Addis Ababa to the coast by train to visit his brother. His first train left on time, but a cow on the tracks delayed it for forty minutes. Because of the delay, he missed his connection at the border town. The station master, a tall woman named Mrs. Kidane, told him the next train would leave at six in the evening. Mr. Abebe spent the afternoon in a cafe near the station, writing postcards and drinking coffee. He finally reached his brother's house late that night.
qs: Where was Mr. Abebe traveling to?
a tall woman named mrs. kidane
What did he do in the cafe?

stories.text: After three days of rain, water began dripping through the ceiling of Kofi's kitchen. He placed a bucket under the leak and climbed onto the roof with his neighbor, Ama, who worked as a builder. They discovered that a strong wind had lifted two of the metal sheets. Ama held the sheets in place while Kofi hammered new nails into the wooden beams. The job took them most of the afternoon. When they climbed down, Kofi's wife Esi had prepared rice and stew for everyone.
qs: through the ceiling of kofi's kitchen
What did Kofi place under the leak?
What had lifted the metal sheets?

stories.text: Sanjay had worked as an elephant keeper at the city zoo for twelve years. His favorite animal was an old female elephant called Rani, who loved bananas and cold showers. One hot afternoon in July, Rani refused to leave the pool, and visitors gathered to watch her spray water at the fence. Sanjay knew that she would only come out for her favorite fruit. He walked to the edge of the pool holding a bunch of bananas above his head. Rani climbed out slowly, and the children in the crowd clapped.
qs: How long had Sanjay worked at the zoo?
When did Rani refuse to leave the pool?
What did Sanjay hold above his head?

stories.text: Mrs. Ortega sold clay pots at the Sunday market in the town square. She had made the pots herself in a small workshop behind her house, and each one was painted with blue birds. A tourist from Canada named Claire wanted to buy four pots, but she worried that they would break on the plane. Mrs. Ortega wrapped each pot in old newspaper and placed them in a strong cardboard box. Claire paid forty dollars and thanked her. Later she sent a photo of the pots standing safely on her kitchen shelf.
qs: What was painted on the pots?
How did Mrs. Ortega protect the pots?
wrapped each pot in old newspaper

stories.text: Liam and his cousin Sofia set out early to climb Grey Peak, a mountain famous for its views. Halfway up, a thick fog rolled in, and they could no longer see the painted marks on the rocks. Sofia remembered that the trail followed a stream, so they listened for running water. After an hour they reached a wooden hut where a park ranger named Mr. Byrne was making soup. He gave them hot bowls and a map, and when the fog cleared they walked back down together.
qs: Why could they not see the marks on the rocks?
that the trail followed a stream
a park ranger named mr. byrne
Where did they find the ranger?

stories.text: Ms. Novak had prepared a presentation for an important meeting with a client from Berlin. Ten minutes before the meeting, her laptop screen turned black and would not start again. Her colleague Tomasz quickly copied the slides from her email onto his own computer. The meeting began only five minutes late. Ms. Novak explained the new project plan clearly, and the client asked many questions about the budget. At the end of the day, the client signed the contract, and Ms. Novak bought Tomasz lunch to say thank you.
qs: How late did the meeting begin?
What did the client ask about?

stories.text: For two months no rain had fallen on Mr. Ndlovu's farm, and the maize plants were turning yellow. Every evening he and his son Sipho carried water from the well to the driest rows. On Friday the radio said that clouds were coming from the east. That night thunder woke the whole family, and rain poured onto the tin roof until morning. Sipho ran outside barefoot and danced in the mud. Mr. Ndlovu smiled, because he knew that the harvest would be saved.
qs: How long had it gone without rain?
Where did they carry water from?
he knew that the harvest would be saved

stories.text: A grey cat named Pepper climbed the tallest oak tree in Rue Lafayette and could not come down. Her owner, an old man called Mr. Girard, tried to tempt her with a dish of sardines, but she only cried louder. A neighbor phoned the fire station. Captain Moreau arrived with two firefighters and a long ladder. She climbed up slowly, spoke softly to the cat, and tucked her inside her jacket. When she reached the ground, Mr. Girard hugged Pepper and invited the firefighters in for coffee.
qs: What did Mr. Girard use to tempt the cat?
Where did Captain Moreau put the cat?

stories.text: Aisha's older sister Fatima was getting married in a garden outside the city. Aisha had the job of carrying the wedding cake from the car to the tent. On the way she tripped over a garden hose, and the top layer slid onto the grass. Her cousin Omar, who was a baker, said he could fix it. He used extra cream and fresh strawberries to cover the damaged side. Nobody noticed anything, and Fatima said it was the most beautiful cake she had ever seen.
qs: in a garden outside the city
What did Omar use to cover the damaged side?

stories.text: Mr. Kowalski had been the town librarian for thirty years. One rainy Monday a woman came in with a book about birds that had been borrowed in 1985. She explained that it had belonged to her late father, Henryk, and she had found it while cleaning his attic. According to the old rules, the fine would have been huge, but Mr. Kowalski only smiled. He stamped the book as returned and put it back on the shelf. Then he asked her to tell him about her father.
qs: How long had Mr. Kowalski been the librarian?
When had the book been borrowed?
Where did the woman find the book?

stories.text: Ms. Adeyemi took her class of twenty-four pupils to the natural history museum by bus. The children were most excited about the dinosaur hall, where a huge skeleton stood beside the staircase. Before lunch, Ms. Adeyemi counted the children and found only twenty-three. A boy named Kwame was missing. They found him in the gift shop, staring at a model volcano. He used his pocket money to buy it, and on the bus home he explained to everyone how volcanoes erupt.
qs: How many pupils were in the class?
Which hall were the children most excited about?
What did he buy with his pocket money?

stories.text: Every summer the village held a horse race across the open grassland. Twelve-year-old Batu rode his family's brown mare, Saran, for the first time. The race was twenty kilometers long and began at sunrise. For most of the way Batu stayed behind the leaders, letting Saran save her strength. Near the finish line he leaned forward and whispered to her, and she galloped past three other horses. Batu finished second, and his grandfather poured milk over the mare's back as a blessing.
qs: Why did Batu stay behind the leaders?
What did his grandfather pour over the mare's back?

stories.text: Mr. and Mrs. Patel were driving across the desert to visit friends in Phoenix when the car began to make a strange noise. Mr. Patel stopped at the side of the road and opened the hood. Steam was rising from the engine, because the radiator had run out of water. They had only one bottle of water left, which Mrs. Patel had bought for the journey. They poured it into the radiator and drove slowly to a petrol station twelve miles away. There a mechanic named Hank fixed a small hole in the radiator hose.
qs: Why was steam rising from the engine?
the radiator had run out of water
radiator had run out of water
Who had bought the bottle of water?
How far away was the petrol station?
a small hole in the radiator hose

stories.text: Hannah Schmidt practiced tennis every morning before school at the courts near the river. Two weeks before the regional tournament, she hurt her wrist while carrying boxes for her father's shop. Her coach, Mr. Alvarez, told her to rest and to practice only her footwork. Hannah was worried, but she followed his advice. On the day of the tournament her wrist felt strong again. She won four matches and lost the final to a girl named Yuki, who later became her doubles partner.
qs: at the courts near the river
How did she hurt her wrist?
while carrying boxes for her father's shop
How many matches did she win?
Who did she lose the final to?

stories.text: Aunt Grace lived in a cottage near the marshes, and every October she counted the geese flying south. This year her nephew Daniel visited from London to help her. They sat in a wooden hide with two pairs of binoculars and a notebook. On the first morning they counted three hundred geese, and on the second morning nearly five hundred. Daniel also spotted a white heron, which Aunt Grace had not seen for many years. She wrote its name in red ink at the top of the page.
qs: in a cottage near the marshes
When did she count the geese?
How many geese did they count on the first morning?

stories.text: Chef Marco Rossi was preparing for a busy Saturday night at his restaurant when he learned that the fish delivery would not come. The supplier's van had broken down on the motorway. Instead of panicking, Marco changed the menu. He made a mushroom risotto, a pasta with lemon and spinach, and a chicken dish with rosemary. His assistant, Giulia, wrote the new dishes on the blackboard by the door. That night the restaurant was full, and several guests asked for the mushroom risotto again the following week.
qs: Why did the fish delivery not come?
the supplier's van had broken down on the motorway
the supplier's van had broken down
Who wrote the new dishes on the blackboard?
Which dish did guests ask for again?

stories.text: A small group of travelers took a wooden boat up the river to visit a village deep in the forest. Their guide, Paulo, pointed out monkeys in the trees and a sleeping caiman on a sandbank. In the afternoon the engine stopped, and the boat drifted toward the bank. Paulo and the boatman, an old man named Jorge, cleaned the fuel pipe with a piece of wire. Within half an hour the engine started again. They reached the village at sunset, where the children welcomed them with songs.
qs: What did they use to clean the fuel pipe?
How long did it take for the engine to start again?
When did they reach the village?

stories.text: The Kim family moved into a new apartment on the fourth floor of a building without an elevator. Most of their furniture went up the stairs easily, but the old piano was too heavy. Mr. Kim called a company that used a crane to lift heavy objects. On Thursday morning a crane lifted the piano through the large balcony window while the neighbors watched. His daughter, Ji-woo, played a short song as soon as it was inside. Mrs. Kim said that the apartment finally felt like home.
qs: Which floor was the apartment on?
What was too heavy for the stairs?
How did the piano get inside?
a crane lifted the piano through the large balcony window

stories.text: Nurse Amina Bello was working the night shift at the hospital when the power suddenly went out. The emergency generator started after a few seconds, but the lights in the children's ward stayed off. Some of the young patients began to cry. Amina gathered them in the playroom, switched on a battery lamp, and read them a story about a brave tortoise. By the time the electrician fixed the problem, most of the children were asleep. In the morning the head doctor thanked her in front of the staff.
qs: What started after a few seconds?
Where did Amina gather the children?
Who thanked her in the morning?

stories.text: Lucas entered a cycling race around the lake with his older brother Mathieu. The course was sixty kilometers long and included a steep hill near the old castle. After forty kilometers Lucas's back tire went flat. He had a spare tube in his bag, but his pump was broken. Mathieu stopped and lent him his own pump, even though it meant losing time. The brothers finished the race together in the middle of the group. Their mother met them at the finish with sandwiches and lemonade.
qs: Why could Lucas not fix the tire alone?

stories.text: Mr. Farouk had sold spices in the old market for forty years. His shop smelled of cinnamon, cumin and dried roses. In the spring he took on a young apprentice named Samir, who wanted to learn the trade. Samir weighed the spices too slowly at first, and customers grew impatient. Mr. Farouk showed him how to judge a hundred grams by the size of the scoop. After a month Samir could serve a customer in less than a minute. Mr. Farouk gave him a brass scale as a gift.
qs: How long had Mr. Farouk sold spices?
What did the shop smell of?
When did Mr. Farouk take on the apprentice?
What gift did Mr. Farouk give Samir?

stories.text: On Wednesday a snowstorm closed every school in the town of Elk River. Emma and her younger brother Noah woke up to find the snow higher than the fence. After breakfast they dug a path to the garage and pulled out their father's old wooden sled. They spent the morning sliding down the hill behind the church. Noah crashed into a snowbank and lost one of his mittens. Emma found it in the afternoon, frozen stiff, and they hung it by the fire to dry.
qs: down the hill behind the church

stories.text: Mr. Svensson, a plumber, was called to a flat where the bathroom sink would not drain. The owner, Mrs. Murphy, said the problem had started after her grandson's visit. Mr. Svensson unscrewed the pipe beneath the sink and found a small plastic dinosaur blocking it. Mrs. Murphy laughed and said her grandson had been looking for that toy all week. The repair took only twenty minutes, so Mr. Svensson charged her for half an hour. She wrapped the dinosaur in paper to post it to the boy.
qs: What was wrong with the sink?
the bathroom sink would not drain
How long did the repair take?

stories.text: Mr. Okonkwo led a group of eight scouts on a camping trip beside Pine Lake. On the first night they cooked beans and sausages over the fire and told stories until late. In the morning they discovered that their bag of bread was gone. Small footprints led from the tent to a hollow log. Inside the log they found a raccoon eating the last slice. The scouts laughed, and Mr. Okonkwo reminded them to hang their food from a tree branch every night.
qs: What did they cook on the first night?
What was gone in the morning?

stories.text: Ravi had studied for weeks for his final chemistry exam at the university. On the morning of the exam, his bus was stuck in traffic because of an accident on the bridge. He got off and ran the last two kilometers through the park. He arrived at the hall just as Professor Lund was closing the doors. Ravi was out of breath, but he sat down and began to write. Three weeks later he learned that he had received the highest mark in his class.
qs: Which subject was the exam in?
because of an accident on the bridge
the highest mark in his class

stories.text: Every autumn Grandpa Hoang made paper lanterns for the children of his street. He used thin bamboo for the frames and colored paper in red, yellow and green. This year his granddaughter Thu asked to make one shaped like a fish. They worked on it for three evenings at the kitchen table. On the night of the festival, Thu carried the fish lantern at the front of the parade. A gust of wind nearly blew out the candle, but she shielded it with her hand.
qs: What did he use for the frames?
What shape did Thu want her lantern to be?
How many evenings did they work on it?
How did Thu protect the candle?
she shielded it with her hand

stories.text: Ms. Dubois flew from Paris to Nairobi for a conference on clean water. When she landed, her suitcase did not appear on the belt. The airline clerk, a friendly man named Otieno, said it had been sent to Johannesburg by mistake. Ms. Dubois had to give her speech the next morning, so she bought a dress and shoes at a market near her hotel. The speech went well, and many people asked for copies of her notes. Her suitcase arrived two days later, on the morning she was leaving.
qs: Where did Ms. Dubois fly from?
Why did she fly to Nairobi?
for a conference on clean water
Where had the suitcase been sent?
What did she buy at the market?
on the morning she was leaving

stories.text: Uncle Pedro kept twelve beehives on the hillside above his orange grove. In June his niece Lucia came to help him collect the honey. He gave her a white suit, gloves and a hat with a net to protect her face. Pedro calmed the bees with smoke from a small metal can before lifting out the frames. One bee crawled into Lucia's glove and stung her thumb, but she kept working. That evening they filled thirty jars with dark orange honey.
qs: How many beehives did Uncle Pedro keep?
on the hillside above his orange grove
the hillside above his orange grove
How did Pedro calm the bees?
with smoke from a small metal can
Where did the bee sting Lucia?
How many jars did they fill?

stories.text: For twenty years Mrs. Evans kept the lighthouse on Gull Island, a rocky place with no trees. Once a week a supply boat brought her food, letters and oil for the lamp. One winter evening she saw a small sailing boat with a torn sail drifting toward the rocks. She flashed the lamp three times and fired a red flare into the sky. A lifeboat from the mainland came within an hour and towed the sailors to safety. The two young sailors visited her the next summer with a cake.
qs: How often did the supply boat come?
What was wrong with the sailing boat?
What did Mrs. Evans fire into the sky?

stories.text: Mr. Adeleke drove a yellow taxi in Lagos. Late one evening, after dropping a passenger at the airport, he found a phone on the back seat. The screen showed many missed calls from someone called Mum. Mr. Adeleke answered the next call and learned that the phone belonged to a student named Chiamaka, who was flying to Accra. He turned around and drove back to the airport as fast as the traffic allowed. Chiamaka was waiting at the departure doors and gave him a hug before running to her gate.
qs: Where did he find the phone?

stories.text: Grandma Vesna asked her twin grandchildren, Ana and Ivo, to paint the garden fence on Saturday. She promised them each a slice of plum cake when the job was finished. Ana painted carefully, but Ivo hurried and splashed white paint on the roses. When a sudden shower started at noon, they covered the wet fence with an old sheet. After the rain stopped, they finished the last part together. Grandma Vesna gave them both two slices of cake, because they had worked so hard.
qs: What did Grandma Vesna ask the twins to paint?
Who splashed paint on the roses?
What did they cover the fence with?
Why did Grandma Vesna give them two slices?
because they had worked so hard

stories.text: Three friends, Nadia, Tariq and Ben, went to explore a cave they had read about in an old guidebook. They brought helmets, ropes and two torches. Deep inside, they found a chamber where the walls sparkled with crystals. On the way back Ben's torch died, and they had to share the other light. Nadia had marked each turn with a piece of chalk, so they found the entrance without trouble. When they climbed out, the sun was setting behind the hills.
qs: How many friends explored the cave?
Where had they read about the cave?
How did they find the entrance?
nadia had marked each turn with a piece of chalk
marked each turn with a piece of chalk

stories.text: Little Kojo was afraid of the dentist, so his father promised to take him to the zoo afterwards. Dr. Mensah, the dentist, had a chair shaped like a rocket and a poster of the planets on the ceiling. She let Kojo press the button that lifted the chair. While she cleaned his teeth, she told him about astronauts who brush their teeth in space. Kojo had no holes in his teeth at all. He left the clinic with a sticker of the moon and a new green toothbrush.
qs: Why did Kojo's father promise to take him to the zoo?
kojo was afraid of the dentist
What was the chair shaped like?
What color was the new toothbrush?

stories.text: Old Tortoise Mbeki kept a brass bell under his shell. One rainy Tuesday morning, Monkey Kito borrowed the bell to wake the village for the harvest. Kito rang it so hard that it flew from his hand and landed in the river. A heron named Sefa fished it out and carried it to the baobab tree by the well. That evening, Tortoise Mbeki found the bell hanging from a low branch. He thanked Sefa with a basket of figs, but he never lent the bell to Kito again.
qs: Who kept a brass bell under his shell?
Why did Kito borrow the bell?
to wake the village for the harvest

stories.text: MILLBROOK, Friday. A painting stolen from the town library last spring was returned on Thursday afternoon. Librarian Mrs. Ines Carvalho said the small landscape arrived in a cardboard box with no return address. Inside the box was a note that read only 'Sorry.' Police Sergeant Tomas Reyes believes the thief lives nearby, because the box was postmarked in Millbrook. The painting, by local artist Hana Okafor, shows the old mill at sunset. It will hang again in the reading room from Monday.
qs: Why does the sergeant believe the thief lives nearby?
because the box was postmarked in millbrook
the box was postmarked in millbrook

stories.text: Dear diary, Saturday. Grandma Yuki gave me her red umbrella this morning because mine broke on Wednesday. I took it to the market with my brother Kenji. We bought three fish and a bag of rice. On the way home the wind snatched the umbrella and blew it onto the roof of the bakery. Mr. Ota, the baker, climbed a ladder and brought it down for us. Kenji says I owe Mr. Ota a drawing, so tonight I will draw him a cat.
qs: Who gave the writer the red umbrella?
How many fish did they buy?
Where did the wind blow the umbrella?
onto the roof of the bakery
What will the writer draw tonight?

stories.text: Long ago in a mountain village, a poor shepherd named Arman found a silver flute in a cave. Whenever he played it, his sheep danced and gave twice as much wool. The greedy Khan heard of the flute and sent soldiers to take it. Arman gave the flute to the soldiers without a fight. But in the Khan's palace, the flute would play only a sad tune, and the Khan's horses ran away. After seven days, the Khan sent the flute back to Arman with a bag of gold.
qs: What did Arman find in the cave?
What did the sheep do when Arman played?
danced and gave twice as much wool
Who sent soldiers to take the flute?
How many days passed before the flute was sent back?
What was sent back with the flute?

stories.text: PORT ELLEN, Monday. Fishermen in the harbour were surprised at dawn when a young seal climbed into Captain Rory MacLeod's boat and refused to leave. The seal, which the crew named Biscuit, slept on a pile of nets for four hours. Marine biologist Dr. Priya Nair came from the university at noon to check on it. She said Biscuit was healthy but tired after a storm. Biscuit slid back into the sea just before sunset, and Captain MacLeod plans to keep a herring in the boat in case it returns.
qs: Whose boat did the seal climb into?
What did the crew name the seal?
How long did the seal sleep on the nets?
When did the seal slide back into the sea?

stories.text: A crow named Odalys found a shiny key in a farmer's yard on Sunday. She hid it in her nest at the top of the pine tree. On Monday the farmer, Señor Ruiz, searched everywhere for the key to his tool shed. A mouse named Pip saw his worry and told Odalys. The crow felt ashamed and dropped the key on the farmer's doorstep at noon. Señor Ruiz never knew who returned it, but he left a dish of corn by the shed every day after.
qs: in her nest at the top of the pine tree
Who told Odalys about the farmer's worry?
What did the farmer leave by the shed?

stories.text: Wednesday night. Professor Adeyemi lent me his old microscope today so I could finish my school project. I carried it home on the bus in a wooden case, holding it on my knees the whole way. My sister Funmi wanted to look at a fly's wing, so we tried that first. Then I looked at pond water from the park and saw tiny creatures swimming in circles. Tomorrow after lunch I must return the microscope to the professor's office on the second floor.
qs: Who lent the writer a microscope?
How did the writer carry the microscope home?
on the bus in a wooden case
What did Funmi want to look at?
Where did the pond water come from?
When must the microscope be returned?

stories.text: In a village beside the Volga lived an old woman called Babushka Olga and her clever goat, Masha. Every winter Olga wove a woollen scarf and sold it at the town fair. One year a fox stole the scarf from her cart while she slept under a birch tree. Masha followed the fox's tracks through the snow to its den. The goat butted the fox until it dropped the scarf. Olga sold the scarf on Saturday for six coins and bought Masha a bucket of apples.
qs: What was the name of Olga's goat?
What did Olga weave every winter?
How many coins did Olga get for the scarf?
What did Olga buy for Masha?

stories.text: RIVERTON, Wednesday evening. The annual pumpkin contest at Riverton Farm was won by eleven-year-old Leila Haddad, whose pumpkin weighed 312 kilograms. Uncle Sami helped her lift it onto the scale with a tractor. Last year's winner, Mr. Gustav Brandt, came second with a pumpkin of 290 kilograms. Leila received a blue ribbon and a new wheelbarrow. She said she will carve a lantern from a smaller pumpkin and give the giant one to the school kitchen for soup.
qs: How much did the winning pumpkin weigh?
Who helped her lift the pumpkin onto the scale?
Where will the giant pumpkin go?

stories.text: A young elephant named Tembo was very proud of his long trunk. Every morning at the lake he sprayed water on the smaller animals just to laugh at them. One hot afternoon, a fire started in the dry grass near the burrow of a hare. Tembo filled his trunk again and again at the lake and put out the flames. The hare, whose name was Kalulu, thanked him and shared his carrots with him. From that day on, Tembo used his trunk to help and not to tease.
qs: Where did Tembo spray water every morning?
What did Kalulu share with Tembo?

stories.text: Monday, 7 a.m. Aunt Rosa called before breakfast to say her parrot, Chico, had escaped through the kitchen window. I ran to her house on Calle Luna with a bag of sunflower seeds. We searched the garden, the church roof and the bus stop. At about ten o'clock, we heard Chico whistling inside the post office. The postman, Mr. Duarte, had found him sitting on a pile of letters. Aunt Rosa hugged Mr. Duarte and promised to fix the window latch tonight.
qs: What did the writer bring to the house?

stories.text: Once in the hills of Connemara there lived a fiddler named Seamus who could not afford new strings. On Midsummer Eve, he played by a fairy ring until midnight. A tiny woman in a green cloak appeared and handed him a golden string. 'Play only for those in need,' she said. Seamus played at weddings for the poor and at wakes for the lonely. When a rich lord offered him a purse of silver to play at his feast, the golden string snapped.
qs: When did Seamus play by the fairy ring?
What did the tiny woman give him?
What was the tiny woman wearing?
What happened when the rich lord offered silver?

stories.text: LAGOS, Tuesday. A lost wallet containing ten photographs and a train ticket was returned to its owner after forty years. Mr. Chidi Eze dropped the wallet at the central station in 1986. Workers repairing a wall found it on Friday behind loose bricks. Station manager Mrs. Funke Ade traced the owner through his name on the ticket. Mr. Eze, now seventy, collected the wallet on Monday morning with his granddaughter Ada. He said the photographs of his late mother were worth more than any money.
qs: How many photographs were in the wallet?
Where did Mr. Eze drop the wallet?
When did Mr. Eze collect the wallet?

stories.text: A spider named Anansi wove a web across the door of the old barn on Thursday night. In the morning, a rooster called Kofi walked straight into it and tore it apart. Anansi was angry, but he said nothing and wove a new web by the window instead. That afternoon, a swarm of flies came in through the window and were caught. Kofi, who hated flies, thanked Anansi. The two became friends, and the rooster always used the door after that.
qs: Where did Anansi first weave his web?
across the door of the old barn
the door of the old barn
Where did Anansi weave the new web?
What was caught in the new web?

stories.text: Thursday evening. Today Uncle Farid took me fishing at the reservoir before sunrise. He let me use his old bamboo rod, the one Grandfather made in Tabriz. I caught two small carp and one big trout. Uncle Farid caught nothing at all, and he laughed about it all the way home. Mother fried the trout for dinner while the carp went into the freezer. Uncle Farid says the rod is mine now, so I hung it above my bed.
qs: How many carp did the writer catch?
Where did the writer hang the rod?

stories.text: A potter named Taro lived at the foot of Mount Kura with his wife, Hana. One winter evening he freed a badger caught in a hunter's snare. The next day a stranger in a brown coat bought every bowl on Taro's shelf with copper coins. On Sunday the copper turned into dry leaves. Hana laughed and swept the leaves into the stove to warm the kitchen. That night, the badger left a sack of rice on their step, and this time it stayed rice.
qs: When did the copper turn into leaves?
What did the badger leave on the step?

stories.text: GREENVALE, Saturday morning. The town's only bus broke down on the bridge over Miller Creek, leaving twenty passengers stranded for two hours. Driver Ahmed Siddiqui said the engine overheated in the summer heat. Mrs. Agnes Holt, who runs the café across the road, brought out lemonade and sandwiches for everyone. A mechanic from Ridgeford, Mr. Paolo Conti, arrived at eleven o'clock and repaired the engine. The passengers gave Mrs. Holt a round of applause before the bus drove on.
qs: Where did the bus break down?
on the bridge over miller creek
Why did the bus break down?
Who brought out lemonade and sandwiches?

stories.text: Two squirrels, Nutmeg and Bramble, found a single walnut under the oak tree on an autumn morning. Each claimed it, and they argued until noon. A wise owl named Oriel offered to settle the quarrel. She cracked the walnut, gave each squirrel half of the shell, and ate the nut herself. 'That is the price of quarrelling,' she said, and flew back to her branch. The squirrels went home hungry, and the next day they gathered acorns together.
qs: How long did the squirrels argue?
What did the squirrels gather the next day?

stories.text: Sunday, late. Today I helped Mrs. Kowalski move her piano from her old flat on Elm Street to her new house by the park. Four of us carried it down three flights of stairs. Her grandson Marek drove the van, and her cat Zosia rode in a basket on the front seat. When we arrived, Mrs. Kowalski played a waltz for us on the porch. She paid me with a jar of plum jam and a promise of piano lessons on Fridays.
qs: Where was the piano moved to?
to her new house by the park
her new house by the park
How many people carried the piano?
What did the writer get paid with?

stories.text: In a dusty town in Oaxaca, a girl named Lupita owned a clay jar that never emptied. Her grandmother had given it to her on her tenth birthday. Every dawn Lupita poured water from it for the thirsty donkeys at the plaza. One dry summer, the mayor, Don Ernesto, demanded the jar for his own garden. The moment it entered his gate, the jar cracked and went dry. Don Ernesto returned the pieces, and Lupita's grandmother mended it with honey and ash.
qs: a clay jar that never emptied
Who did Lupita give water to every dawn?

stories.text: OSLO, Thursday. A pair of red mittens left on a tram in January has finally found its owner. Tram driver Ingrid Solberg kept the mittens in her locker for nine months. Last week she posted a photo of them in the window of the tram depot. On Wednesday afternoon, a teacher named Lars Berg recognised them as a gift his mother had knitted for his daughter, Sigrid. Sigrid, now eight, wore the mittens to school this morning even though it was not yet cold.
qs: What was left on the tram?
How long did the driver keep the mittens?
Where did she post a photo of them?
in the window of the tram depot
the window of the tram depot

stories.text: A peacock named Raja spent every morning admiring his tail in the pond. A plain brown sparrow, Chotu, built nests and sang for the farmers. When the monsoon came on a Friday, the heavy rain soaked Raja's tail, and he could not fly up to the banyan tree. Chotu showed him a dry hollow under the temple steps. Raja waited there for three days until the storm passed. Afterwards he spent less time at the pond and more time with Chotu.
qs: Where did Raja admire his tail?
Who built nests and sang for the farmers?
Where did Chotu take Raja to shelter?
a dry hollow under the temple steps
How many days did Raja wait there?

stories.text: Tuesday, after school. Our teacher, Mr. Okonkwo, brought a tortoise named Duchess into class this morning. He has borrowed her from the city zoo for one week. Duchess is sixty years old and eats lettuce, cucumber and hibiscus flowers. At lunch, Amara and I fed her a slice of cucumber, and she ate it very slowly. On Friday afternoon, Mr. Okonkwo will drive her back to the zoo in his blue car. I am going to miss her.
qs: Who brought the tortoise to class?
What did the writer and Amara feed her?
How will Duchess go back to the zoo?

stories.text: In a fjord village there lived a blacksmith named Eirik who forged the sharpest axes in the north. One stormy night a troll knocked on his door and asked for an axe. Eirik agreed, but only if the troll fetched a sack of coal from the mountain before dawn. The troll ran up the mountain and back, but the sun rose as he reached the forge. He turned to stone in Eirik's yard. The blacksmith kept the coal and used the stone troll to hang his horseshoes on.
qs: the sharpest axes in the north
What did Eirik ask the troll to fetch?
What happened to the troll when the sun rose?
Where did the troll turn to stone?

stories.text: KYOTO, Sunday. A temple bell missing since the spring festival was found on Saturday evening in a rice field outside the city. Farmer Hiroshi Tanaka noticed the bronze bell while checking his water gates. Head priest Reverend Kenji Mori said thieves probably dropped it because it was too heavy to carry far. Six volunteers carried the bell back to Kofuku Temple on Sunday morning. The priest rang it at noon, and many neighbours came out of their homes to listen.
qs: in a rice field outside the city
a rice field outside the city
Why did the priest think thieves dropped it?
because it was too heavy to carry far
it was too heavy to carry far
How many volunteers carried the bell back?

stories.text: A fox named Rusty boasted to the hens that he could open any gate. On Tuesday night, he tried the gate of Farmer Brown's coop, but the farmer had tied it shut with a new rope. Rusty chewed the rope for an hour, until his teeth ached. At dawn the farmer's dog, Blue, woke and chased him across the meadow. Rusty hid in a hollow log until the sun was high. After that he boasted much less and chewed much more carefully.
qs: What did Rusty boast he could do?
Whose coop did Rusty try to open?
How had the gate been shut?

stories.text: Friday, 9 p.m. Today Professor Lindqvist asked me to deliver a sealed envelope to the museum before five o'clock. I cycled across the city in the rain with the envelope inside my jacket. At the museum, a guard named Mr. Haddad would not let me in until I showed my student card. The curator, Dr. Elena Sokolova, opened the envelope and smiled. She said it held the professor's notes on a Roman coin. She gave me a museum pass, so I will visit on Sunday.
qs: Who asked the writer to deliver an envelope?
Where did the writer keep the envelope while cycling?
What did the guard want to see?
the professor's notes on a roman coin
When will the writer visit the museum?

stories.text: Long ago, a girl named Mei lived with her father, a poor fisherman on the Li River. One morning his net brought up a jade comb instead of fish. Mei combed her hair with it, and her hair grew long and shone like the river at noon. A merchant offered fifty silver coins for the comb, but Mei refused. That autumn, when her father fell ill, she traded the comb to a doctor for medicine. Her father recovered, and her hair stayed long and shining.
qs: What did the net bring up?
How much did the merchant offer for the comb?
Why did Mei trade the comb?
Who did Mei trade the comb to?

stories.text: BRISTOL, Monday. A grey parrot that went missing from a pet shop on Park Row was found three days later in a dentist's waiting room. Receptionist Mrs. Joan Patel said the bird flew in through an open window on Friday morning and sat on the coat rack. It greeted every patient with 'Good morning!' Shop owner Mr. Bilal Khan arrived with a cage at lunchtime. He said the parrot, called Captain, had learned the greeting from the shop's radio.
qs: How did the parrot get in?
What did the parrot say to every patient?
Who came to collect the parrot?

stories.text: A camel named Zahra carried salt across the desert for her master, old Hamid. One evening a lizard asked to ride on her saddle as far as the oasis. Zahra agreed, though the lizard was very talkative. At midnight the lizard saw a sandstorm coming and warned Zahra. She knelt behind a dune, and Hamid wrapped himself in his blanket beside her. When morning came, they reached the oasis safely, and Hamid gave the lizard a fig.
qs: What did Zahra carry across the desert?
Where did the lizard want to go?
When did the lizard see the sandstorm?
What did Hamid give the lizard?

stories.text: Saturday morning. Cousin Tariq arrived from Karachi last night with a suitcase full of gifts. He gave Mum a green silk shawl and gave Dad a book of old maps. For me there was a wooden kite painted like a tiger. After breakfast we flew the kite on the hill behind the library. The string broke, and the kite landed in Mr. Doyle's apple tree. Mr. Doyle shook the branch until it fell, and we gave him two of Tariq's sweets.
qs: Where did Cousin Tariq arrive from?
What was the kite painted like?
How many sweets did they give Mr. Doyle?

stories.text: High in the Andes, a llama herder named Inti owned a small drum made from a gourd. When he beat it at dusk, the llamas came home from the far pastures. One night a condor stole the drum and carried it to its nest on the cliff. Inti's sister, Killa, climbed the cliff before sunrise and found the drum among the condor's eggs. She left a woven blanket in its place to keep the eggs warm. The condor never troubled the herders again.
qs: What was Inti's drum made from?
When did Inti beat the drum?
What did Killa leave in place of the drum?

stories.text: HAVANA, Wednesday. A 1957 car belonging to taxi driver Miguel Ortega rolled into the harbour on Tuesday night after its handbrake failed. No one was inside. Divers from the port authority pulled the blue car out of the water at six o'clock on Wednesday morning. Mr. Ortega's neighbour, Señora Carmen Vidal, said he had driven the car for thirty years. He hopes to have it running again within a month with the help of his son, Julio.
qs: Whose car rolled into the harbour?
Why did the car roll into the harbour?
Who pulled the car out of the water?
How long had he driven the car?
Who will help him repair the car?

stories.text: A goose named Greta laid one golden egg every Sunday for a farmer's wife, Mrs. Abernathy. Mrs. Abernathy sold each egg at the Monday market and bought bread and wool. Her neighbour, Mr. Crabb, offered to buy Greta for a whole cart of hay. Mrs. Abernathy refused, saying a steady egg was better than a sudden heap of hay. Mr. Crabb went home grumbling. The goose kept laying, and the farmer's wife never went hungry.
qs: How often did Greta lay a golden egg?
What did Mr. Crabb offer for Greta?

stories.text: Wednesday, midnight. I could not sleep, so I climbed to the roof with Grandpa Nikos's telescope. He keeps it in a leather bag behind the kitchen door. I pointed it at the moon and saw craters like the holes in Grandma's cheese. Then my neighbour Eleni waved from her balcony and asked to look. We took turns until the clouds rolled in at one o'clock. In the morning I put the telescope back before Grandpa Nikos woke up.
qs: Whose telescope did the writer use?
in a leather bag behind the kitchen door
a leather bag behind the kitchen door
What did the craters look like?
Who asked to look through the telescope?
When did the clouds roll in?

stories.text: In the city of Isfahan, a carpet seller named Yusuf owned a small rug that could fly only on Thursdays. Every Thursday he flew it to the market in Shiraz to buy saffron. One Thursday night a thief named Karim stole the rug from his shop. Karim sat on it on Friday morning and shouted for it to fly, but it lay still. A crowd gathered and laughed, and the city guard caught him. Yusuf got his rug back and gave the guard a jar of saffron.
qs: Which city did Yusuf live in?
On which day could the rug fly?
Why did Yusuf fly to Shiraz?

stories.text: DUBLIN, Friday. A library book borrowed in 1974 was returned this week with a letter of apology and a cheque for the late fee. The book, a guide to Irish birds, was posted by Mrs. Maureen Doherty from her home in Boston. In her letter, she explained that she packed it by mistake when her family emigrated. Librarian Mr. Declan Walsh said the fine was waived and the cheque would go to the children's reading club. The book is now on display beside the front desk.
qs: Where was the book posted from?

stories.text: A tortoise named Moshe and a hare named Pinto agreed to share a cabbage patch. Pinto ate the leaves quickly every morning, while Moshe ate only the ones he needed. By Friday the hare had finished his half and began to nibble Moshe's. Moshe said nothing but planted new seeds each evening. When winter came, Pinto had nothing left, and Moshe's half was full of young cabbages. He invited the hare to dinner, and Pinto never nibbled again.
qs: What did Moshe and Pinto agree to share?
When had Pinto finished his half?
What did Moshe do each evening?
Who did Moshe invite to dinner?

stories.text: Sunday evening. Auntie Grace came to visit after church and brought her famous banana bread. She left her reading glasses on our sofa when she went home at four. Mum asked me to take them to her flat on Victoria Road. I rode the number 12 bus and found Auntie Grace trying to read a letter by holding it far from her face. She laughed when she saw the glasses. Then she gave me two more slices of banana bread for the trip home.
qs: What did she leave on the sofa?
Which bus did the writer ride?
How many slices did she give for the trip home?

stories.text: In a village in the hills of Gangwon, a kind farmer named Dae-ho mended the broken wing of a magpie one spring morning. The magpie flew away in autumn and returned the next April with a pumpkin seed in its beak. Dae-ho planted the seed beside his gate. By harvest time the vine had grown three huge pumpkins. When he cut them open, he found rice, silk and a pair of silver shoes inside. He shared the rice with every family in the village.
qs: the broken wing of a magpie
What was in the magpie's beak?
How many pumpkins grew on the vine?
Who did Dae-ho share the rice with?
